about: Edits that can strand a player. "risk" is "lock" (can leave the file impossible to finish) or "loss" (something is permanently missed; the game can still be finished). "riskWhen" is the dangerous direction: "set" (turning a flag on / raising a number), "clear" (turning it off / lowering it) or "both". "flags" entries are stamped onto every field in any tab that edits the same save bit; "fields" entries name one field by its key. A field can also carry "risk", "riskWhen" and "riskWhy" itself. The editor asks before making such a change; it never blocks it.
source: Preset soft-lock audit and guardrail draft by Muse, 15 November 2026. The reasons are inferences from how the game grants rewards, not tested cases.

flags.name: Extra Wallets
flags.why: Lowering the count takes Extra Wallets away for good: Beedle keeps his own record of what he sold and doesn't sell them again (checked in Sky Recomp: with the count lowered to 2, his stock stayed sold out).

flags.name: Extra Wallet obtained
flags.why: Clearing this while Extra Wallets are owned leaves the save unlike any the game writes. Beedle won't sell them again either way.

dungeons.skyviewBoss.why: Marking the boss as defeated by hand can permanently skip what beating it gives you, such as its Heart Container.

dungeons.skyviewKeys.why: The small-key count has to agree with the doors already unlocked in this dungeon. Too few keys for the doors still locked can leave the dungeon impossible to finish.

dungeons.skyviewBossKey.why: The game sets the boss key and the boss door together. Changing one without the other can leave the boss room unreachable.

dungeons.skyviewBossDoor.why: The game sets the boss key and the boss door together. Changing one without the other can leave the boss room unreachable.
